title: Matignon's Cipher-3, 1586: two Poitou intelligence notes (BnF fr. 15572 f. 276, fr. 15571 f. 179) and a six-page despatch to the King (fr. 15573 ff. 379-381)

steps.what: Located the two Cipher-3 leaves on the images: fr. 15571 f. 179 at canvas 187 left (bound upside down; first listed as 'f. 178v, fourth hand') and fr. 15572 f. 276 at canvas 285 right; siblings ff. 277r-278r deciphered in ff. 279-280.

alejandrozarco (PR #25): Tomokiyo's partial Cipher-3 table checked by hard-EM alignment of a blind transcription of sibling f. 277r against its contemporary decipherment on ff. 279-280; values added (### = et, two-stroke # = i, dotted v = u, S-shape = q and others).
alejandrozarco (PR #25): f. 276 (22 lines) and fr. 15571 f. 179 (21 lines) transcribed sign by sign twice, independently; reads agree on 93.8% (f. 276) and 91.5% (f. 179) of signs.

alejandrozarco (PR #25): f. 276 deciphered with the Cipher-3 key, 698/734 signs (95.1%) in lexical runs (fr-henri4 word list); f. 179 transcribed and checked against Tomokiyo's unpublished magenta interlinear decipherment, 466/509 (91.6%). Poitou faction report naming La Rousiere, la Mare, Iehan Durant, Lansac.

Review of PR #25: measure.py re-run reproduces 698/734 and 466/509; 50 shuffled keys give median 6.3% / 3.1% (max 21.5% / 21.0%); line structure of f. 276 L01, L21, L22 and f. 179 L18 (blot), L21 checked on the Gallica natives.

alejandrozarco, after the PR #25 review: measure.py and control_shuffle.py now take their lexicon from the shared lang/ model fr-1600-letters (corpora.text + lm.norm 'early', words >= 20 occurrences) instead of bundled word lists, which are removed. f. 276 706/734 (96.2%; 50 shuffled keys median 6.9%), f. 179 473/509 (92.9%; median 3.5%); the difference from the word list is mainly 'veullent' reaching 20 occurrences under lang normalisation. f. 276 L18 read as 'redoute la [K]; quelque chose', making the C-with-epsilon sign q and K a one-sign code word (paix? Ligue? Royne?).

Split from the former combined target matignon1586 under the one-key rule (George Lasry, 14 Oct 2026): the two Cipher-3 leaves are their own entry; f276/ and f179/ moved here. measure.py re-run on both read_final.txt files reproduces 706/734 and 473/509.

Contributed (Brett Burford, issue #44, v0.1-v0.5 18-19 Oct 2026): fr. 15573 ff. 379r-381v, 2,836 signs read by Claude Opus 5.5 under a sign sheet, five passes voted, corrections decided on the image; Tomokiyo's Cipher-3 key checked on ff. 277-280 and extended from the 1585 letter fr. 15570 ff. 271-273; two-valued signs chosen by whole words. His measure: 0.90-0.95 of signs per page in French words, shuffled 0.59-0.78; 5 short runs and 5 rare code signs open.

Re-measured here with this entry's rule (f276/scripts/measure.py, fr-1600-letters, 20 shuffled keys) on his signs through his recorded key choices (f379_381/to_read.py): f. 379r 440/503, 379v 447/490, 380r 420/492, 380v 493/532, 381r 479/524, 381v 261/295 = 2,540/2,836 (89.6%); shuffled medians 5.8-9.8%, max 33%. View 740 compared with his f. 379r signs: 22 cipher lines as he has them, and the opening signs of l. 2 (b, a, a hooked sign, 30) correspond.

outcome.method_basis: f. 276 and fr. 15573 ff. 379-381 were deciphered with Tomokiyo's partial Cipher-3 table, checked and extended on deciphered siblings (ff. 277r/279-280; fr. 15570 ff. 271-273); f. 179 was transcribed blind and reconciled with Tomokiyo's interlinear decipherment.

parts.label: f. 276
parts.basis: Tomokiyo's Cipher-3 table, checked on ff. 277r/279-280 and extended (### = et and other values); 706 of 734 signs (96.2%) in sense runs, measured; 50 shuffled keys median 6.9%

parts.label: fr. 15571 f. 179
parts.basis: Tomokiyo's interlinear decipherment in magenta on his image of the leaf, checked by two blind sign-by-sign readings with his key; 473 of 509 signs (92.9%), measured; shuffled median 3.5%

parts.label: fr. 15573 ff. 379r-381v
parts.basis: Brett Burford (issue #44): Tomokiyo's Cipher-3 table with values from the 1585 deciphered letter fr. 15570 ff. 271-273, five voted LLM reader passes; 2,540 of 2,836 signs (89.6%) in sense runs, measured here; 5 rare code signs and 5 short runs open

outcome.fraction_read_source: f276/scripts/measure.py (lang model fr-1600-letters, the targets/matignon1586/measure.py rule): f276/read_final.txt 706/734, f179/read_final.txt 473/509, f379_381/read_<page>.txt 2,540/2,836 (Burford v0.5 through to_read.py); 3,719 of 4,079 signs, 21 Oct 2026

gaps.item: f. 276 L18 'K' and L14 'C with o inside', one-sign code words not in Tomokiyo's table
gaps.detail: Each occurs once (paix? Ligue? Royne? for K); neither recurs on these two leaves; the deciphered Cipher-3 siblings f. 189/190, f. 282 and fr. 15570 ff. 271-273 have not been searched for them.

gaps.item: f. 179 L13, the omega-with-overbar code sign (a person, Navarre?)
gaps.detail: One occurrence; Tomokiyo's magenta at 680 px does not settle it.

gaps.item: blots: f. 276 L04 after 'de lui', f. 179 L18 after 'en'
gaps.detail: Ink blots on the leaf; checked on the Gallica natives.

gaps.item: f. 276 L22 closing (one or two signs before the plaintext 'ou...'), f. 179 L20 'de la D[...]use' and a struck sign, and a few short spans
gaps.detail: Faint or struck signs at the edge of the slip; the rest of the 28 + 36 unread signs are words the period lexicon holds fewer than 20 times (prieure, escriuent).

gaps.item: fr. 15573 ff. 379-381: five rare code signs (barred double o where not le roy de Navarre, the circle on a cross, the looped epsilon with a stroke, the zigzag-tailed 3, the m with a z-like tail)
gaps.detail: Each occurs once to three times and in none of the deciphered Cipher-3 letters Burford checked (fr. 15572 ff. 189-190, 277-280, 282; fr. 15573 f. 373; fr. 15570 ff. 271-273).

gaps.item: fr. 15573 ff. 379-381: about 300 signs outside sense runs (5 short runs of clear signs Burford could not read, doubtful words, smudged signs)
gaps.detail: Mostly names, period spellings and reader errors (0.93-0.96 per sign on known text); Burford's v0.5 list (f379_381/burford/unresolved-v0.5.md) explains 110 of 115 items; the 5 unexplained runs are clear on the image and may be names or code. A sign-by-sign human check has not been made.

outcome.notes: Contributed by alejandrozarco (PR #25, 6-7 Oct 2026), reviewed and re-measured here. Content: a Poitou intelligence note on the Catholic factions round La Roussière (f. 276) and a sibling naming Pons, sickness in the army and Lansac for the sea army (f. 179). 21 Oct 2026: Brett Burford's reading of fr. 15573 ff. 379-381 (issue #44) added as a third part; measured here 89.6%.
